shared_elements: low-relief carving on a stone surface with rounded rectangular panel format
profile-oriented figures (a human head in A, animals/birds in B)
circular disc motif (chest disc/ear ornament in A; disc held by the animal in B)
bands of repeated parallel/angular incised lines
justification: Both are shallow relief carvings on a rounded-cornered rectangular stone field that combine profile figures with a plain circular disc and zones of repeated linear/angular incision, which is the most concrete correspondence. But A is a single, tightly framed human bust rendered in smooth, evenly incised contour lines filling the whole panel, whereas B is a large pillar with stacked registers of modelled animal bodies and a zigzag band, so composition, subject and carving manner differ fundamentally.
